bib.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models. Huiqiang Jiang, Qianhui Wu, Chin-Yew Lin, Yuqing Yang, Lili Qiu (Microsoft). EMNLP 2023, pp. 13358–13376 (arXiv 2310.05736).

COVERAGE: Read all 70,575 of 70,575 chars across 19 PDF pages: body, limitations, Appendix A–E and every case-study figure. References were skimmed. Page numbers below are PDF pages (proceedings page minus 13357).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: On GSM8K, 20x compression costs about 1.5 EM.
  number: 77.33 vs 78.85 EM (117 vs 2,366 tokens)
  setup: Target model GPT-3.5-Turbo-0301 with greedy decoding, temperature 0. The small model is Alpaca-7B. The original prompt is Fu et al.'s 8-shot complex CoT. "Quarter-shot constraint".
  quote: "Ours 77.33 117 20x" / "Full-shot 78.85 2,366 -" / "up to 20x compression with only a 1.5 point performance drop"
  where: Table 2, p6; Conclusion, p9
- claim: At lower compression it matches or slightly beats the full prompt.
  number: GSM8K 79.08 at 5x; BBH 70.11 vs 70.07 at 3x; 14x costs 1.44
  setup: 1-shot constraint; half-shot for the 14x figure
  quote: "Ours 79.08 446 5x" / "Ours 70.11 288 3x" / "the EM scores will decrease by 1.44 and 1.52, respectively, despite compression ratios as high as 14x and 20x"
  where: Table 2, p6
- claim: BBH degrades much more than GSM8K.
  number: -8.5 EM at 5x, -13.2 EM at 7x
  setup: BBH 3-shot CoT, GPT-3.5-Turbo
  quote: "On BBH, our approach achieves compression ratios of 5x and 7x with the EM score decreasing by 8.5 and 13.2 points"
  where: p6
- claim: The baselines collapse at high compression.
  number: Selective-Context 44.20 at 15x; GPT-4 compression 56.33 at 20x
  setup: GSM8K quarter-shot. Selective-Context used the same Alpaca-7B.
  quote: "Selective-Context 44.20 157 15x" / "GPT4 Generation 56.33 188 20x" / "lower than ours by 33.10 points at a compression ratio of 20x"
  where: Table 2, p6; p7
- claim: End-to-end latency falls, and the compressor itself is cheap.
  number: 8.6 s to 4.9/2.3/1.3 s at 2x/5x/10x (1.7x to 5.7x faster); compression alone takes 0.8/0.3/0.2 s
  setup: GSM8K on one V100-32G
  quote: "End-to-End w/o LLMLingua 8.6" / "2.3(3.3x) 1.3(5.7x)" / "can achieve a speedup ranging from 1.7x to 5.7x"
  where: Table 6, p8
- claim: Conversation and summarisation tasks compress less while BERTScore F1 stays high.
  number: ShareGPT 3.3x, BS-F1 87.70; Arxiv 9x, BS-F1 89.03
  setup: BLEU, ROUGE and BERTScore measured against GPT-3.5-Turbo's own outputs as references. 575 ShareGPT samples; 500 arXiv papers (first five sections, each cut to 10k chars).
  quote: "Ours 19.55 40.81 22.68 30.98 87.70 177 3.3x 13.45 44.36 24.86 34.94 89.03 176 9x"
  where: Table 1, p6; App. A.1, p12
- claim: Iterative token-level compression and the budget controller do most of the work. Distribution alignment adds little.
  number: Without ITPC 72.93; without budget controller 73.62; without alignment 78.62 (vs 79.08); stop-word removal reaches only 1.3x
  setup: GSM8K, 1-shot
  quote: "- w/o Iterative Token-level Prompt Compression 72.93 453 5x" / "- w/o Distribution Alignment 78.62 452 5x" / "- w/ Remove Stop Words 76.27 1,882 1.3x"
  where: Table 3, p7
- claim: Using GPT2-small as the compressor costs about 1–2 EM.
  number: 77.02 / 76.42 / 76.27 at 5x / 14x / 18x
  quote: "a performance drop of 2.06, 0.99, and 1.06 EM points"
  where: Table 5, p8
- claim: The method transfers to Claude-v1.3, tested in only two settings.
  number: 83.51 at 5x, 82.61 at 14x, vs Simple Prompt 81.8
  quote: "Ours in half-shot constraint 82.61 171 14x"
  where: Table 4, p8
- claim: Estimated compute saving of about 4x at 5x compression. This is analytical, not measured.
  number: c ≈ 0.264·L·c_LLMs
  setup: Assumes the small model gets the same serving optimisations as the LLM, and a 7B/175B parameter ratio.
  quote: "we can achieve nearly 4x savings in computational resources when using the smaller LM with a prompt compression rate of 5x"
  where: p8
- claim: Compressed prompts are hard for humans to read, but GPT-4 can reconstruct them (GPT-3.5 cannot).
  number: none
  quote: "LLMs can effectively comprehend the semantic information in the compressed prompts, even if it might be challenging for humans"
  where: p9, footnote 9
- claim: Compression also shortens the outputs.
  number: none
  where: Fig. 2, p8
- claim: Dollar savings.
  number: GSM8K $5.2 to $0.5
  quote: "cost reductions of $4.7, $8.0, $0.4, and $0.8"
  where: Table 7, p12
- claim: Hyperparameters.
  number: k=2, τ_ins=0.85, τ_que=0.9, segment size 100
  where: p5

LIMITS: Performance drops sharply at 25x–30x on GSM8K (Fig. 3). The authors say the upper limit varies with prompt length, task type and number of sentences. The small model's tokenizer can differ from the target LLM's, which leads to underestimating token length (p10). The paper has no retrieval or RAG evaluation and no long-context QA. The target models are 2023 API models (GPT-3.5-Turbo-0301, Claude-v1.3). Claude was tested in only two settings "Due to the limitation of API cost". ShareGPT and Arxiv are scored against GPT-3.5's own generations. The compressor is not question-aware. Latency comes from one GPU and one dataset.

BUILDS ON: Selective-Context (Li, 2023) is the direct predecessor. Also credited: Shannon (1951) on redundancy; Gilbert et al. (2023); gist tokens (Mu et al., 2023); AutoCompressors (Chevalier et al., 2023); ICAE (Ge et al., 2023); perplexity-based OoD detection (Wu et al., 2023); Alpaca (Taori et al., 2023); CoT prompts from Fu et al. (2023b).

CODE: None worth keeping. Algorithms 1–2 are pseudocode (p4). Code is at https://aka.ms/LLMLingua.

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p3) shows the framework: a 2,366-token prompt becomes 117 tokens, which is the pipeline at a glance. Fig. 3 (p9) plots EM against compression ratio for every method, and shows the cliff and how far each method holds up faster than Table 2. Fig. 4 (p14) shows a compressed prompt next to GPT-4's reconstruction, which makes "unreadable to humans" concrete.

PROBLEMS: Equations 4–5 came out of extraction garbled; the prose around them was readable. The PDF contains no embedded instructions. The repo has no source PDF for LongLLMLingua or LLMLingua-2, so I could not check anything against those papers.

---
AUDIT OF REPO CITATIONS

1. generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/notes/06-generation-for-rag.md:234 (LLMLingua row)
- "A small LM (Alpaca-7B)": CORRECT. Quote: "Selective-Context ... We use the same small LM, i.e., Alpaca-7B" (p6). The paper also uses GPT2-Alpaca.
- "drops low-perplexity tokens, segment by segment, under a per-section budget": CORRECT, but it leaves out the coarse step. The budget controller first keeps whole demonstrations in descending order of perplexity (Alg. 1, p4).
- "On GSM8K chain-of-thought prompts for GPT-3.5-Turbo, 20× compression cost 1.5 EM points (77.3 vs 78.9)": CORRECT (Table 2, p6). The setup would be clearer with "an 8-shot, 2,366-token prompt cut to 117 tokens".
- "end-to-end latency fell from 8.6 s to 2.3 s at 5× on one V100": CORRECT (Table 6, p8).
- "Selective context scored 44.2 at 15×": CORRECT ("Selective-Context 44.20 157 15x", Table 2).
- "Tested on prompts and conversations, not retrieved passages": SETUP MISSING. It omits BBH and the arXiv long-document summarisation task. The "not retrieved passages" part is right.
- Omitted: the BBH loss (-13.2 at 7x), which would stop readers generalising from GSM8K; and the cliff at 25–30x.
- Replacement: "| LLMLingua | A small LM (Alpaca-7B) first drops whole low-perplexity demonstrations, then drops low-perplexity tokens segment by segment under a per-section budget. On an 8-shot GSM8K chain-of-thought prompt for GPT-3.5-Turbo, 20× compression (2,366 → 117 tokens) cost 1.5 EM points (77.3 vs 78.9), where Selective Context scored 44.2 at 15×. On BBH, 7× cost 13.2 points, and every method collapses at 25–30×. End-to-end latency fell from 8.6 s to 2.3 s at 5× on one V100. Tested on reasoning prompts, conversations and arXiv summaries, not retrieved passages ([arXiv:2310.05736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05736), Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023) |"

2. Same file :235 (LongLLMLingua row: "Question-aware version: compresses and reorders documents using both context and query"): NOT IN PAPER. 2310.05736 never mentions LongLLMLingua, reordering or question-aware compression. The row has no citation, and no source for it is in the repo. Nothing in it is misattributed to 2310.05736 because it carries no numbers. It needs its own source, read and cited, or the label "(*Building AI Agents*, ch. 6)" only.

3. Same file :233 (Selective context row): uncited. The description is consistent with how LLMLingua describes it ("self-information of each lexical unit (such as sentences, phrases, or tokens)", p1). "Keep the top percentile" is not in this paper.

4. generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/references.md:66: CORRECT on every number: 20×/1.5 EM/GPT-3.5-Turbo, 8.6 → 2.3 s at 5×, "not tested on retrieved passages", EMNLP 2023. You could add "BBH loses 13.2 EM at 7×".

5. ai-engineering/02-context-engineering/notes/05-compression-compaction.md:227 ("Token pruning (LLMLingua-style) | ... | 2–5× with modest loss on many tasks; output is unreadable to humans"): UNCITED / NOT IN PAPER for the range.
- LLMLingua reports 3x–20x, not 2–5×.
- "Modest loss on many tasks" is overstated for BBH (-8.5 at 5x) and understated for GSM8K (-1.5 at 20x).
- "Unreadable to humans" is supported (p9).
- Suspicion, unverified: the 2–5× range looks like LLMLingua-2's headline (arXiv 2403.12968, which reports 2x–5x as I remember). No PDF of that paper is in the repo, so check it before you keep the range.
- Replacement: "| **Token pruning** (LLMLingua) | A small LM drops low-perplexity tokens under a per-section budget | On GSM8K chain-of-thought prompts for GPT-3.5-Turbo, 20× cost 1.5 EM, but on BBH 7× cost 13.2. Output is hard for humans to read, though GPT-4 can mostly reconstruct it ([arXiv:2310.05736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05736), Jiang et al., EMNLP 2023) |"
- Under the sharpens rule, adding this citation also needs a references row in ai-engineering/02-context-engineering/references.md, which has no LLMLingua row now. That file's existing PDF links point across pillars (e.g. ../../generative-ai/...), so the row can link to generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/jiang-2023-llmlingua.pdf.

6. There are no LLMLingua mentions in any deck.yaml. scripts/papers/ledger.jsonl:668 holds the entry for this paper.
